clue.text: The shipwrecked sailor found a path

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
a way is a path or route

explanation.surface: A sailor washed ashore discovers a track across the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the verb for casting metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone marooned after a wreck is the classic example of a person left stranded on a desert island.

indicators.note: the covering word is wrapped round the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: a cape is a covering cloak
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snack served in a little wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A canape is a small savoury bite served before a meal with drinks.

clue.text: Pledge to install running water in an animal shelter

indicators.note: to install one thing in another is to put it inside

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, so a stretch of running water

explanation.surface: A promise to plumb a water supply into a pigpen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a North Yorkshire river; crosswords often call a river 'running water'.
explanation.definitionFit: A surety is a guarantee or security given as a promise.

indicators.note: the pungent word goes about, around, the a

parts.note: acrid means sharp and pungent

explanation.surface: A small creature with a strong smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An acarid is any mite or tick, of the order Acari.

definitions.meaning: an expression that things are as before

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unchanged, identical as before, and also serves as nevertheless.

indicators.note: says the letters of the word Croats could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Performers who might hail from Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors are players in the theatrical sense, people who perform roles on stage.

definitions.meaning: a dated, now offensive term for a person from China
in cricket, a delivery by a left-arm wrist spinner that turns into a right-hander

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game; this delivery is the left-armer's version of an off-break from wrist spin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old, now offensive term for a man from China and also a type of left-arm spin delivery in cricket.

parts.note: over means on top of, topping
a shoe is the basic footwear

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an outer layer over everyday clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A galosh is a protective covering worn over a normal piece of footwear.

parts.note: the main is the sea, so a lawn in the sea is underwater meadow plants

explanation.surface: Asking which is the principal part of a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like principal; in crosswords 'the main' is the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine flowering plants form meadows on the shallow ocean floor, like a lawn underwater.

parts.note: a norm is a standard or model to follow
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: Normally a fashion model brings along a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean as a rule, in the ordinary course of things.

clue.text: He was long ago nailed by a lady killer

definitions.text: He was long ago nailed by a lady killer

parts.words: He was long ago nailed by a lady killer
parts.note: a biblical general whom Jael killed by driving a tent peg through his temple while he slept

explanation.surface: An ancient man was done in by a murderous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady killer' suggests a womaniser; here it is literally a woman who killed. The story is in Judges 4.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Judges the Canaanite commander fled to Jael's tent, where she hammered a peg into his head.

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
the Conservatives (Tories) are the party of the political right

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the Conservative ranks have it correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a mistake is to fix or amend it, a verb sense.

clue.text: An old Roman taking care as ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, so the words care and as are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Roman of old behaves cautiously, as he has been told.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius was the most famous bearer of this Roman family name, later a title of emperors.

clue.text: They'll make no effort to move

definitions.text: They'll make no effort to move

parts.words: They'll make no effort to move
parts.note: people carried in a vehicle travel without doing any of the work

explanation.surface: Lazy people who won't budge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests idlers who refuse to move; they do move, but someone else does the driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers carried by a bus or car are conveyed without exertion of their own.

clue.text: Up and down they go endlessly

definitions.text: Up and down they go endlessly

parts.words: Up and down they go endlessly
parts.note: moving stairways in shops and stations whose steps circulate without stopping

explanation.surface: Something that rises and falls without end, like a yo-yo.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving staircases carry people up or down on a continuous loop of steps.

indicators.note: foolish suggests the words green and are made into nonsense, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Being naive and silly poses a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put at risk, imperil.

clue.text: Work quietly when in pain, taking breaks

indicators.note: the work and quiet letters go when, or once, inside the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
OP is short for opus, a work
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone working on silently despite pain, but pausing now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping means halting or pausing, as when taking rests.

clue.text: He's left beasts without a role to play

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the beasts go round the role

parts.note: deer are beasts
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A man has walked out on his animals, having nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A departer is one who goes away, someone who has gone.

clue.text: The lowest entrap the female majority

parts.note: to net something is to catch or entrap it
her is the female pronoun
most means the greater part, the majority

explanation.surface: A depressing note: the women caught in the trap are the most downtrodden.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means furthest down, the bottom-most of all.

parts.note: a state is a condition

explanation.surface: Asking whether an old coin is in decent shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Some American GIs never back an old officer

indicators.note: back means the hidden run is read backwards
some of the letters of the words American GIs never are taken

explanation.surface: American soldiers never support a former commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'American GIs never' backwards gives REVENSIGNACIREMA, with the answer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensign was formerly the lowest commissioned rank of infantry officer, who carried the colours.

parts.note: not grabbing a snack but acquiring the means of biting, as a baby does

explanation.surface: Grab a quick snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like having a snack; read as 'get the bite with which to eat', it means a baby cutting its teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants develop their first set of dentures, which gives them something to chew food with.

indicators.note: says the word for Pop is read backwards

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, as is pa
a peal is the ringing of bells

explanation.surface: Asking Dad to come home and phone, if you would.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to plead or beg, as one does when saying please.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a stance is a position or point of view

explanation.surface: Majority opinion offered as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or illustration, much like a sample.

parts.note: IT is an abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letters, is taken out of the word Tory, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Conservative is depressed by a Mediterranean merger but stays resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Gritty means resolute and determined, showing grit or courage.

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again, repeatedly
strict means rigid or inflexible

explanation.surface: Something persistently stiff because of a muscle spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp, as a verb, is to hamper or confine, to limit someone's freedom.

clue.text: Look at some fish in colourful surroundings

indicators.note: the fish sits in the colourful word, which surrounds it

parts.note: red is a colour, so stands for colourful
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Watching some fish among bright coral.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to gaze at or observe it.

indicators.note: the letters of gear sent are wrongly placed and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking to recall equipment that was dispatched by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate, to make someone withdraw their affection or keep apart.
